name: Performance Expectations and Fairness

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests whether expectations, continuous feedback, formal reviews, support, and calibration form a consistent and fair performance system.
positioning.productLabel: No-Surprise Performance Lens — based on Claire Hughes Johnson's public Scaling People materials
notAClaimOf: one review cycle fitting every company

attribution.display: Product synthesis based on Claire Hughes Johnson's public performance-management discussions

neutralParaphrase: A defensible performance system establishes role-relevant expectations in advance, provides timely specific feedback and support, and makes formal review a synthesis rather than a surprise. Product use additionally requires privacy, accessibility, consistency, bias review, and authorized human judgment.

locator.value: p. 2, lines 149-154: feedback and performance mechanisms and the no-surprise review test
Lines 21-25: expectations ahead of time, empathy, support, people development, and business results
Lines 68-75: lightweight fundamentals, continuous feedback, and more structure for inexperienced managers
Transcript lines 218-223: task/behavior focus, self-assessment, owned observations, specificity, and a plan

requiredConditions: The company has employees with recurring role expectations.
Only authorized, purpose-limited, privacy-safe evidence is used.
Individual decisions remain with trained, accountable humans under applicable law.

requiredEvidence.description: Role outcomes, level expectations, goals, behaviors, quality standards, and evidence that they were communicated in advance.
Authorized records of timely specific feedback, recipient input, coaching, resources, accommodations, and follow-up.
Review schedule, evidence period, reviewer roles, calibration, employee response, appeal or correction, and decision ownership.
Lawful, sufficiently powered audit of rating patterns, manager severity, promotion, improvement support, accommodations, and adverse outcomes with confounder review.

decisionQuestions: Were the relevant expectations known before the review period?
Did ongoing feedback identify the same issues and offer support?
Can the employee respond, correct evidence, and appeal process errors?
Are similar roles and evidence treated consistently across managers?
What possible bias, accommodation, role change, or resource constraint explains the outcome?
positiveSignals: Expectations are role-specific, observable, and communicated in advance.
Formal reviews synthesize prior feedback rather than introduce new criticism.
Employees can add context and challenge factual errors.
Calibration checks evidence quality and inconsistent standards.
Support and accommodations are documented before adverse action.
redFlags: Ratings rely on likability, style, presence, or vague culture fit.
Managers apply materially different standards without review.
Protected-trait proxies or AI-inferred traits enter the process.
The company lacks recourse, privacy controls, or accountable decision ownership.
disconfirmingEvidence: An unexpected event concerns newly discovered fraud, safety, or integrity evidence and follows a lawful investigation.
Small group differences are too underpowered to interpret and remain unknown rather than exonerating the process.
Different role standards are documented and job-relevant.
A low rating follows repeatedly documented expectations, feedback, support, and unchanged work outcomes.
contraindications: Do not automate ratings, promotion, discipline, termination, or employability judgments.
Do not analyze protected traits or infer them from proxies.
Do not expose individual records to investors or unauthorized users.
Do not treat no surprise as sufficient proof of fairness.
Do not deploy without legal, privacy, accessibility, and fairness review.

instructions: Map expectations, communication, feedback, support, review, calibration, recourse, and authority.
Audit an authorized sample for expectation-to-feedback-to-review continuity.
Separate evidence quality, manager severity, role context, accommodation, and possible bias.
Keep individual decisions outside the model.
Conclude system coherent, emerging, inconsistent, unsafe, or insufficient.

sourceReliability.medium: Authorized review samples and process records.
sourceReliability.high: Longitudinal records, independent audit, legal review, and employee recourse evidence converge.

evidenceStrength.high: Repeated system evidence plus independent consistency and fairness review.

evidenceCoverage.high: Communication, support, accommodations, calibration, recourse, fairness, privacy, outcomes, and counterevidence covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Formal performance decisions materially affect workforce and execution.

judgmentConfidence.medium: Several authorized cases support a bounded system judgment.
judgmentConfidence.high: Longitudinal, audited, privacy-safe evidence supports the conclusion.

promotionRequirements: Obtain legal, privacy, accessibility, and fairness review.
Validate minimum cohorts and audit methods.
empiricalQualifications: Performance data are shaped by role assignment, manager behavior, resources, and historical bias.
Small samples and missing records limit inference.

rights.notes: Public author materials are paraphrased; no performance template or rubric is reproduced.

openIssues: This card cannot leave research status before licensed and employment-domain review.
